text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's Austrian newspapers:
- Siemens' Austrian train-making unit SGP-Verkehrstechnik's Vienna subsidiary has secured its survival as Siemens has handed over decision making for passenger and underground trains to SGP.

- Andreas Khol, chief whip of the conservative coalition partner, said Joerg Haider's far-right Freedom Party is not fit to govern. He remains in favour of the current coalition although he demands far-reaching reforms.
- Austria's new insurance giant combining Bundeslaender and Austria Collegialitaet is to withdraw from real estate and property management.
- Belgian investor SPRL Choppinet Claubert is taking legal action against Investmentbank Austria, accusing it of leading the Belgian astray over the issue of Vindobona Privatbank shares.
- Analysts at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell have revised up their profit estimates for Creditanstalt for 1996 and 1997 by ten percent each following good earnings in the first nine months of 1996.
- Economic research institute IHS chief Bernhard Felderer says investing in the education of the young workforce is more profitable than further education of over 50-year-olds.

- Rubber maker Semperit, majority owned by Creditanstalt, has invested over one billion schillings in Thailand over the last five years to create the world's largest medicinal glove producer. The company expects record pre-tax earnings of at least 150 million schillings this year.
- The Vienna bourse has already gone into hibernation and analysts see activity on the exchange remaining lacklustre this week.
- Oesterreichische Volksbanken AG is to open a subsidiary in Zagreb in the near future. It is also still in the race for Upper Austria's Hypo bank.
